notes: The exchange is stateless per request: handle_request dispatches on the verb and returns immediately, with no session, handshake, or teardown, so `states` is empty (kvstore/src/api.rs:15-33).

`timeouts` is empty deliberately. The `put` verb carries a `ttl_secs` field, but it is only formatted into the stored value string (`format!("ttl={ttl_secs}")`, kvstore/src/api.rs:27-28); nothing in the code expires entries or moves the exchange on elapsed time. Modelling it as a protocol timeout would be inventing behaviour the source does not have.

The transport is thin: the CLI calls handle_request directly rather than reading a socket or stdin (kvstore-cli/src/main.rs:8-11). It is modelled as a protocol because kvstore/src/api.rs defines and documents a request grammar and a response vocabulary for untrusted input ("Handle a wire request of the form `verb:arg[:arg]`. Wire requests are untrusted input.", kvstore/src/api.rs:12-14) — that wire format, not the function call, is the protocol.

kvstore/src/storage.rs (FileStore) is not a participant. It reads and writes files under a root directory and can render an outcome as a Response (kvstore/src/storage.rs:33-39), but no code path in this revision connects it to handle_request or to the CLI, so it exchanges nothing with another party here.
kvstore/src/cache.rs is the store's internal state, not a separate participant — it is reached only through handle_request (kvstore/src/api.rs:19, 28).

protocol.framing: one request per argument string, colon-separated fields (`verb:arg[:arg]`)

messages.name: put:<key>:<ttl_secs>
messages.schema: put:<key>:<ttl_secs>  (ttl_secs parsed as u64; value stored is the literal string `ttl=<ttl_secs>`)

messages.name: Response::Ok(<value>)
messages.schema: Ok(String) — cached value for the requested key

messages.name: Response::Stored
messages.schema: Stored — acknowledgement of a successful put

participants.description: Collects request strings from the process arguments, submits each one to the store in order, and prints the debug rendering of each response to stdout.
participants.name: cli-client

participants.description: Parses each request as `verb:arg[:arg]`, serves `get`/`put` against the bounded in-memory cache, and answers with a Response variant. Treats requests as untrusted input.
participants.name: store

protocol.transport: cli argv in, stdout out (one request string per argument, handled in-process by kvstore::handle_request)
